title: Sub-Scope Detail Delete Delivery
summary: add a manage-only Delete action for one validated displayed sub-scope document with exact preview, confined apply, targeted rebuild, and list reconciliation
content_html:
Sub-Scope Detail Delete Delivery

Status And Order

Started as SSI-2, after Sub-Scope Report Contribution Delivery. SSI-2.1 is complete and paused at its review gate. The existing Delete endpoints, capability payload, management client, mutation service, and child rebuild path now support the frozen singular target. No visible Delete action or report reconciliation behavior has changed.

SSI-2 is the first new user workflow in the feature. It proves the detail toolbar, exact-target mutation, local rebuild, route repair, and inventory reconciliation path before selection and package preparation widen the collection surface.

Complete Outcome

Manage mode shows Delete in the detail toolbar on the same header row as Back only after docs_subscope has validated and rendered one listed document.

Delete previews and, after explicit confirmation, removes exactly:

{ scope, sub_scope, doc_id }

It rebuilds only the affected child collection, removes subdoc from the URL with replacement history, reconciles the management inventory, and returns to the list. Public mode has no button and does not load the controller, delete client, modal, or mutation workflow.

Change Classification

kind work
shipped and retained main-index Delete workflow and confirmation patterns; managed target resolver; sub-scope builders; report detail validation
extended document-delete client, capability, service planning/apply, activity, and rebuild support an exact sub-scope target
refactored shared delete mechanics may be extracted where parent and child mutations genuinely share behavior
genuinely new rendered sub-scope detail Delete action and its collection-local reconciliation

This is not sub-scope lifecycle deletion and must not reuse the capability that deletes an entire configured sub-scope.

UI And Target Contract

  • The button exists only in a validated detail state.
  • Loading, failed, unknown, unlisted, list, and unmounted states have no Delete target.
  • The button label, confirmation title, preview rows, and focus return identify the exact document.
  • Confirmation defaults focus to Cancel.
  • Cancel leaves the detail and URL unchanged.
  • The workflow never derives a target from the URL, selected parent document, title, focused row, or Tag Registry association.
  • Normal success emits no redundant status message; blockers, stale state, unavailable data, and errors remain visible.

The Delete implementation is manage-owned and lazy. The shared report only provides the validated target and toolbar host.

Service And Mutation Contract

Preview and apply retain one exact normalized target. Apply re-resolves the source after confirmation and rejects a stale or changed target before writing.

For a sub-scope document:

  • resolve only the configured one-level child source root;
  • require source filename/front-matter identity agreement;
  • reject multiple IDs and hierarchy expansion;
  • delete only that one canonical Markdown source;
  • never inspect or alter the parent scope's default document;
  • rebuild the child manifest and by-ID projection;
  • do not rebuild the parent index-tree, Recent, or global search;
  • retain scope, sub_scope, and doc_id in preview, result, and activity; and
  • never read or update Studio JSON.

The existing parent-scope Delete contract remains unchanged. Shared mechanics must not force parent hierarchy/default-document semantics into the flat child collection.

There is no sub-scope search builder or child search output in the shipped configuration. The sub-scope rebuild helper runs only the child document builder, and its service-used --skip-browser-config flag is valid only with a sub-scope build. Adding a child search subsystem is not part of Delete; future sub-scope search adoption belongs to the overall Docs Viewer search surface.

Independent Ownership

An external reference is not a blocker. Deleting a tag document may leave a stale Tag Registry doc_id; that is allowed by Independent Canonical Documents.

Preview and apply use exact doc_id; title is display data and does not participate in mutation validation.

The parent document that loads docs_subscope is only a presentation host. Ordinary parent-scope Delete may remove that document under the existing parent hierarchy contract, but it does not delete the registered report module, configured sub-scope, or any child document. A configured child with no report host and a registered report module with no loading document are both valid.

In Scope

  • One manage-only Delete button in the validated detail header.
  • Capability-aware availability and busy state.
  • Write-free preview, explicit confirmation, stale-target revalidation, and exact apply.
  • Confined source deletion and targeted child rebuild.
  • URL replacement, detail teardown, inventory reconciliation, and list return.
  • Exact-target identity, cancel, failure, and retry behavior.
  • Focused client, service, mutation, activity, report-controller, public isolation, and realistic UI evidence.

Not In Scope

  • Bulk or checkbox-backed Delete.
  • Deleting the report parent, Tag Registry record, tag alias, or configured sub-scope.
  • Cascade, synchronization, association repair, or delete prevention based on external references.
  • Choosing or navigating to a replacement document.
  • Parent index reload or sidebar selection change.
  • Undo, Trash, archive, or filtering.

Frozen SSI-2.0 Contract

Authorities

concern current owner SSI-2 stance
exact child target docs_management_document_target.py reuse { scope, sub_scope, doc_id } normalization, configured-child resolution, direct-child confinement, and filename/front-matter agreement
parent Delete docs_management_mutations.py and /docs/delete-* retain the existing { scope, doc_ids[] } subtree/default-document behavior without interpreting report metadata or cascading to a sub-scope
child write/rebuild docs_management_mutation_service.py and docs_write_rebuild.py use the existing sub-scope mutation-plan branch with singular delete compensation, but run only the child docs builder
browser client docs-viewer-management-client.js add singular target-aware methods; retain the existing plural parent methods
capability management capability service and browser capability helpers add document_delete: { preview, apply, sub_scope_detail }; a missing or false field keeps the detail action unavailable
detail target and host shared docs-subscope-report.js plus the manage contribution accept only the already validated detail target; do not read subdoc or selected parent state
confirmation management modal shell reuse explicit confirmation with Cancel initially focused
activity docs_management_context.log_event through the mutation plan retain the exact target and singular deleted ID

Request Boundary

The existing endpoints remain the mutation family. Their request shapes become a strict union:

parent preview: { scope, doc_ids }
parent apply:   { scope, doc_ids, confirm: true }

child preview:  { scope, sub_scope, doc_id }
child apply:    { scope, sub_scope, doc_id, source_revision, confirm: true }

The parent branch and responses do not change. Presence of sub_scope selects the singular child branch, whose allowed keys are exact. doc_ids, tag_id, association data, fallback IDs, and other extra fields are rejected rather than ignored.

Preview And Result

Child preview returns:

operation: preview
target: { scope, sub_scope, doc_id }
scope, sub_scope, doc_id
title
source_revision: sha256:<canonical source bytes>
allowed, blockers, warnings
delete_count: 1
delete_documents: [{ doc_id, title, path }]
generated_outputs: [child manifest rebuild, exact by-ID removal]

Confirmed apply repeats the exact target, revision, deleted source path, deleted_doc_ids: [doc_id], delete_count: 1, child rebuild diagnostics, and summary. It carries no parent hierarchy, descendant, default-document, Studio, or external-association fields.

A failed rebuild response repeats the target and reports source_restored, recovery_rebuild, and retry_safe; it never presents a failed attempt as a completed deletion.

Stale Proof

Preview hashes the resolved canonical Markdown source. Apply:

  1. normalizes the strict child request;
  2. re-resolves the configured child and exact direct-child source;
  3. rechecks filename/front-matter identity;
  4. compares the current source revision with the confirmed preview revision;
  5. rejects missing, moved, mismatched, unconfigured, or changed source before writing; and
  6. only then plans one source deletion.

A stale revision is a conflict, not a fresh implicit preview. The browser keeps the detail visible and requires a new preview. Confirmation never authorizes a different current source merely because the same doc_id still resolves.

Rebuild And Failure Boundary

The committed mutation removes one Markdown source under the configured child root, using the existing child watch-suppression owner, then runs:

build_docs.py --scope <scope> --sub-scope <sub_scope> --write --diagnostics \
  --skip-browser-config

That builder reconciles the child manifest and removes the stale exact by-ID payload. SSI-2.1 adds the explicit service-used browser-config suppression and removes the separate parent-search command, so this path does not write the parent index tree, Recent, parent search, public projection, or browser configuration.

The singular source unlink is atomic. If the child builder fails, the service atomically restores the exact confirmed source bytes, reruns the same confined child builder to reconcile derived outputs, and returns a structured error without activity success. The response states source restoration and recovery rebuild outcomes. A restored source keeps the same revision receipt, so retry repeats the same exact-target validation; no broad repair or parent rebuild is introduced.

Test-Owned Fixture Matrix

case fixture expectation
ordinary one synthetic child source and a sibling; only the target source and by-ID payload disappear
missing exact child source absent; preview/apply reject without writes
mismatched filename doc_id differs from front matter; resolver rejects
unconfigured child valid-looking child ID absent from scope config; resolver rejects
multiple/broadened doc_ids, nested/path-escape ID, association fields, or extra target keys reject
cancel preview succeeds; modal cancellation sends no apply request and retains URL/detail
stale source source bytes change after preview; apply conflicts and deletes nothing

All destructive route and browser evidence must create its own temporary configured scope/sub-scope and canonical sources. The Analysis tags collection is a manual read/review surface only.

Delivery Tracker

[x] SSI-2.0 — Freeze Exact Delete Semantics

  • [x] Trace the existing parent Delete client, planner/apply, confirmation, capability, activity, and rebuild owners.
  • [x] Trace the managed sub-scope target resolver and child build entrypoints.
  • [x] Define the exact preview/result shapes and stale-target proof.
  • [x] Freeze a test-owned ordinary, missing, mismatched, unconfigured-child, cancel, broadened-target, and stale-source fixture matrix.
  • [x] Confirm that no parent hierarchy/default-document rule is valid for the child mutation.

Review gate: approved before SSI-2.1 implementation.

[x] SSI-2.1 — Extend Preview And Apply

  • [x] Add target-aware client and service entry without changing existing parent Delete requests.
  • [x] Reuse the central managed-document resolver.
  • [x] Implement write-free preview and confirmed exact apply.
  • [x] Add suppression, atomic deletion, child rebuild, response, diagnostics, and activity behavior.
  • [x] Prove that multiple IDs, path escape, stale source, and external association payloads cannot broaden the mutation.

Review gate: paused after service evidence deleted one synthetic child and only its derived child outputs.

SSI-2.1 Evidence

  • test_docs_management_subscope_delete.py drives the actual child builder against a temporary configured scope. It removes one target source and by-ID payload, rewrites the child manifest, retains a sibling, and proves byte stability for the parent Index, Recent, search, and three browser configs.
  • Focused Python selections passed 109 tests across the new service, existing parent mutation/apply, target resolver and source-revision flow, rebuild helper, child builder, capability, service-config, and public-runtime boundaries, including an exact CRLF-byte revision receipt.
  • The focused sub-scope report module smoke passed the exact target/revision request projection and parent-target rejection.
  • Explicit Python and JavaScript lint passed for every changed source and test path. git diff --check passed.
  • Independent diff review found no compatibility alias, public import leak, or new documentation, lint, or type-boundary adoption trigger.
  • Analysis tags was not mutated or used for destructive evidence. No visible report action, confirmation workflow, URL repair, or list reconciliation was exercised because those remain SSI-2.2.

SSI-2.2 must freeze whether successful report reconciliation removes the exact row from the already loaded inventory or refetches the inventory. The server rebuild remains required either way. Main Index Delete currently reloads the index; the main Index local projection precedent belongs to Move.

[ ] SSI-2.2 — Add The Detail Workflow

  • [ ] Contribute Delete only for a validated detail target.
  • [ ] Lazy-load its client/workflow and reuse the existing confirmation modal contract.
  • [ ] Reconcile successful deletion to list state with replacement history and the exact row absent from the inventory projection.
  • [ ] Preserve the parent index, report selection, and unrelated caches.
  • [ ] Cover cancel, blocker, stale-state, service-unavailable, rebuild-failure, retry, Back/Forward, and unmount behavior.

Review gate: manually review ordinary exact-target preview states, narrow header layout, focus, and recovery.

[ ] SSI-2.3 — Isolation And Closeout

  • [ ] Run focused target, mutation, service route, controller/module, report, public read-only, and targeted-build checks.
  • [ ] Use synthetic test-owned sources for destructive route/browser evidence.
  • [ ] Confirm the public import graph excludes Delete implementation modules.
  • [ ] Run the maintained Docs Viewer profile at the integration boundary.
  • [ ] Independently review source/generated effects and record untested surfaces.
  • [ ] Transfer only the shipped exact-delete contract to durable owners.

Completion Gate

SSI-2 is complete only when one validated child can be deleted without touching another document, external canonical data, the parent index, or the public runtime.
